title: Second effect: multiple loss of intenseness of inherent faith, hope, and charity
source_text: LI. Secundum effectum peccati gravioris, quod mortale appellat, & quo dif-ferre dicit a peccatis levioribus, quae venialia dicuntur, est multiplex gratiae per Spiri-tum Sanctum nobis inhaerentis amissio. Quamvis enim per peccata etiam graviora, non omnino deleantur & tollantur, juxta ipsum, habitus fidei, spei, & charitatis, multum tamen per illa minuuntur & debilitantur, idque non tantum, ut ait, extrin-sece quoad fervorem & facilitatem, seu promptitudinem his habitibus utendi; sed etiam intrinsece, quoad ipsam eorum entitatem. Habent enim, inquit, hi habitus sufficientem latitudinem, intra quam sicut de facto augentur, ita etiam remitti possunt per actus contrarios.
pass_a_gloss: The second effect of the heavier sin which he calls mortal, and by which he says it differs from lighter sins called venial, is a manifold loss of the grace inherent in us through the Holy Spirit. For although through even heavier sins the habits of faith, hope, and charity are not altogether destroyed and taken away, according to him, yet they are much diminished and weakened by them—and that not only, as he says, extrinsically as to fervor and facility or readiness in using these habits, but also intrinsically as to their very entity. For these habits, he says, have a sufficient latitude within which, just as in fact they are increased, so also they can be remitted through contrary acts.
pass_b_english: Second mortal effect: grace inherent by the Spirit is multiply diminished.
Faith, hope, and charity habits are not erased, yet weakened outwardly in fervor and inwardly in entity—within a latitude that contrary acts can remit.

lemmas.gloss: habits of faith, hope, and charity

choices.why: Habit remains; intensity and entity suffer.
